newsitem.title: USA: Regional bells make ADSL deal with Alcatel.
newsitem.headline: Regional bells make ADSL deal with Alcatel.

text.p: Alcatel Telecom, a unit of Alcatel Alsthom, said on Friday it reached agreement with Ameritech Corp, BellSouth Corp, Pacific Bell and Southwestern Bell on multi-year contracts for asymmetric digital subscriber line, or ADSL, equipment.
The separate contracts address the individual needs of the four companies. Terms of the agreements were not disclosed, Alcatel said.
Under the agreements, the companies will buy the Alcatel 1000 ADSL system to use to deliver ADSL-based services to consumers and businesses.

The companies started contract talks with Alcatel in early October, the company said. Although they worked together on the bid process, each has its own proprietary marketing plans and deployment schedules.
All four companies currently have ADSL service trials underway.
ADSL technology uses existing copper telephone wiring to allow customers to interact with data networks and the Internet on a portion of the existing phone line.
Alcatel said the companies expect this technology to serve thousands of their customers within the next year to 18 months, and could be in use by more than a million customers by 2001.
